Title: Queue and BFS Route Finder
Summary: Build a queue, shortest-distance search and parent-based route reconstruction that handles cycles and unreachable destinations.
Overview:
Build a shortest-route inspector for an unweighted colony graph. It prints the shortest distance and one deterministic route, or a clear unreachable result. This is the correct tool for one ant's minimum travel time and a lower bound for many ants.

Reuse P04's canonical graph. You will build a queue with a head index, discover vertices once and reconstruct a path from parents. The artifact deliberately stops before claiming that one shortest route is an optimal multi-ant plan.

Refresher:
BFS explores all vertices at distance k before distance k+1. Each tunnel costs one turn for one ant, regardless of coordinate length. Set a vertex's parent and distance when it is discovered, then enqueue it once.

queue := make([]int, 0, len(g.Adj))
head := 0
// Your search owns discovery and enqueueing.
// Advancing head avoids repeatedly removing index zero.

Use a sentinel such as -1 for undiscovered distance or a separate seen slice. A parent value of 0 cannot by itself mean undiscovered because vertex 0 is real. Path reconstruction walks destination → parent → source and then reverses that list. An unreachable destination has no parent chain to follow.

BFS gives an O(V+E) search with an O(V) queue and metadata. Enumerating all simple paths is potentially exponential and is unnecessary for this task.
Spec:
1. Implement Shortest(g,start,end) returning one path including both endpoints and its edge count. Validate indices and adjacency integrity.
  2. Use P04's sorted neighbors so equal-length route selection is deterministic. Mark discovery before enqueueing.
  3. For start==end return a one-vertex path and distance 0 in this general-purpose tool. The final colony grammar requires distinct terminals.
  4. For an unreachable target return a distinguishable error and no path. Ordinary cycles and disconnected extra rooms must not cause nontermination.
  5. Path length in edges equals len(path)-1; every consecutive pair must be adjacent. Bound reconstruction to V parent steps to detect a broken invariant.
  6. The CLI's JSON has Names, Links, Start and End. Print distance=D path=name,name,.... Coordinates do not affect route choice.
  7. Include queue tests and a justification of shortestness using distance layers. This tool does not allocate multiple ants or promise minimum completion turns for them.

Components.Title: Build the discovery queue
Components.Goal: Create a traversal worklist with explicit visited semantics.
Before: Why must a vertex be marked before enqueueing?
What does the queue contain after a vertex is expanded?
Steps: Initialize distance/seen and parent arrays for all vertices.
Use a slice plus head index instead of repeated front deletion.
Record queue operations in a small hand trace before implementing neighbor traversal.
Components.Hint: In a diamond s-a-t and s-b-t, t must enter the queue once even though two edges discover it.
Components.Trace: For neighbors a then b, trace queue [s], then [s,a,b], then discovery of t from a. b must not enqueue t again.
Components.Gate: A cycle and a diamond each enqueue no more than V vertices.

Components.Title: Search distance layers
Components.Goal: Find reachability and the shortest edge count.
Before: What does distance[v] certify when v is dequeued?
When can the algorithm stop while preserving the route result?
Steps: Store predecessor and distance together at first discovery.
Return a specific unreachable result if the worklist empties without the destination.
Components.Hint: For one-edge tunnels there is no weight relaxation loop. Replacing the queue with a stack invalidates the same shortestness argument.
Components.Trace: Compare s-a-t with s-b-c-t. The two-edge route must win even if a's coordinates are far away.
Components.Gate: Tests cover a direct edge, unequal routes, equal routes, cycles and an unreachable target.

Components.Title: Reconstruct and certify a route
Components.Goal: Convert predecessor metadata into a trustworthy artifact.
Before: How will you distinguish no route from a zero-length route?
Steps: Walk parents from end toward start with a V-step guard.
Independently check endpoints, adjacency and edge count before formatting names.
Components.Hint: Keep route validation separate from discovery. A parent assignment bug should be visible even if a distance happens to be correct.
Components.Trace: With parents t←a←s, reconstruction first yields [t,a,s], but the printed path is s,a,t and distance is 2.
Components.Gate: A deliberately broken parent cycle is rejected by the reconstruction guard; a valid route passes an independent edge check.

Run:
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go run . testdata/routes.json
Verification:
The fixture contains the two-edge route s-a-t and the three-edge route s-b-c-t. Expect distance=2 path=s,a,t.

  • Direct s-t: distance 1 and path [s,t].
  • Diamond with equal routes: stable choice through lexically earlier neighbor a.
  • Disconnected t: unreachable error and no route.
  • Triangle on the way to t: terminate with the shortest route, never loop.
  • General-purpose start==end: distance 0 and one endpoint.
  • For every returned route, independently check all edges and len(path)-1.

Exit gate

Explain shortestness by BFS layers, show at most one discovery per vertex and state why this is only a lower bound for multiple ants.
Engineering: What exactly makes BFS shortest: the visited set, the queue or both?
Which changes would be required if tunnels had unequal travel times?
Why is a reconstructed path a useful certificate even when distance is the requested output?
Can early stopping on discovery and on dequeue produce the same distance with different metadata completeness?
Why is a map-backed neighbor order a reproducibility risk?
How would a malformed parent chain reveal a search invariant failure?
What does a single-ant shortest path fail to describe about multi-ant traffic?
Practical: Swap coordinate values in your colony parser data and confirm BFS is unchanged.
Add a cycle around a dead-end branch.
Count queue insertions on a diamond.
Check every returned edge using a separate helper.
Change equal-route input order and confirm stable output.
Extras: Return all distances from one source. Use them for later pruning without enumerating paths.
Count shortest routes on a small graph. Decide how to handle integer overflow.
Add a distance-to-end precomputation for time-layer pruning in P09.
Benchmark line, star and grid graphs with the same vertex count.
Compare bidirectional BFS on large sparse graphs. Preserve the route and tie-breaking contract before considering it an optimization.
